frequency_question: How often does major federal voting eligibility legislation pass both chambers and reach enactment or final passage within a single congressional session?
membership_rule: Includes major standalone federal election law overhauls focused on voter registration requirements or franchise rules; excludes routine appropriations riders, minor technical amendments, and non-binding resolutions.
coverage_note: 4 named major legislative pushes covering the primary modern attempts to overhaul federal voter registration standards.
known_gaps: Earlier historical civil rights voting acts (e.g., 1965, 1970) are excluded due to radically different legislative rules (e.g., pre-cloture dynamics) and party alignments.
skeleton: Major voting eligibility bills reaching floor consideration in polarized political environments
multiplier: 2 hits out of 4 major attempts in closely divided or polarized eras
validity_reason: Valid until the next congressional configuration and Senate rule changes alter the legislative bottleneck.
